prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell). Airports: Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport (keep safety authority). Elements: Demand Prediction Service (DPS, Marlinstone; unconstrained demand); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM; AAR=Airport Acceptance Rate); Slot Allocation Engine (SAE, Blueharbor; CTT=Calculated Takeoff Time); Departure Metering Service (DMS, Emberline; optional Passenger Misconnect Count). DPS/CAM/SAE/DMS reject data lacking Time Synchronization Service timestamp. Airport CDM Portal; Identity Access Service (IAS); Audit Event Ledger; Alert Distribution Hub (Digital Briefing Room); Performance Analytics Warehouse (delay absorption, adherence, emissions); Collaborative Decision Log; Business Rules Registry; Tower Sequence Manager; Ramp Movement Board; North/South Runway Meter; East/West Apron Sensor; Surface Surveillance Adapter; Weather Ingest Gateway; Flight Data Exchange (Flight Intent Message, realized times); Airline Interface Adapter; Handling Resource Planner; Sector Load Monitor; Common Situation Display; Contingency Operations Console; Arrival Regulation Console; Post Operations Report; Airport Capacity Plan. Silverpine grants emergency access only after IAS records incident reference/expiry. Actors: Airline Operations Coordinator (TOBT=Target Off Block Time), Aircraft Operator Representative (submit Flight Intent Messages, challenge via Decision Log); Regional Flow Manager (RFM); Slot Coordinator; Data Governance Steward; Meteorology Briefing Officer; Airport Duty Manager (ADM; Capacity Plan, mode changes); Tower Supervisor; System Support Engineer; Ramp Control Lead (Board never replaces visual checks/radio); Ground Handling Dispatcher; Network Operations Liaison; Airspace Sector Planner; Emergency Response Coordinator; Deicing Coordinator. Training: classroom, supervised practice, shadowing; recurrent annually/after major changes; multi-function simulations covering all mode transitions; users compare automation with local knowledge, log decisions and deviations in Decision Log; assessments verify detecting stale data, time sync problems, duplicate flights, conflicting constraints, over-reliance; post-exercise reviews use Warehouse and Ledger, assign owners. Human factors: workload monitoring, alert prioritization, consistent terminology, confirmations for high-impact actions, no silent mode changes; workstations compare Display/Portal/Sequence Manager/Ramp Board without manual copying. Modes: Normal Operations; Adverse Weather Mode; Capacity Reduction State; Recovery Phase; Slot Compliance State; Contingency Fallback State (ADM declares after consulting RFM). Deployment:

New part:
S895: Readiness Gate 2 shall confirm that the Flight Data Exchange, Airline Interface Adapter, Surface Surveillance Adapter, and Weather Ingest Gateway can be connected without disrupting existing airport operations.
S896: Readiness Gate 3 shall confirm that local procedures have been mapped to the Airport CDM Portal, Tower Sequence Manager, Ramp Movement Board, Departure Metering Service, and Arrival Regulation Console.
S897: Readiness Gate 4 shall confirm that training, shadow operations, contingency procedures, and operational acceptance criteria have been completed before live collaborative decisions are made through the Regional Flow Platform.
S898: Interface certification shall be performed separately from operational acceptance so that technical conformance defects do not become unresolved procedural issues.
S899: Each interface shall be tested for message structure, time stamping, identity attribution, replay handling, duplicate detection, outage recovery, and rejection behavior under degraded network conditions.
S900: The Demand Prediction Service, Capacity Assessment Module, Slot Allocation Engine, Gate Conflict Detector, Sector Load Monitor, North Runway Meter, and South Runway Meter shall be certified against agreed reference scenarios before they are used for operational recommendations.
S901: Certification results shall be recorded in the Collaborative Decision Log when they affect operational procedures and in the Audit Event Ledger when they affect access, configuration, or transaction traceability.
S902: Airport onboarding shall start with data discovery workshops that identify local tools, manual workarounds, unofficial spreadsheets, and locally maintained constraint registers.
S903: The migration plan shall classify each local tool as retired, retained for read-only reference, integrated through an approved interface, or replaced by a Regional Flow Platform function.
S904: No local tool shall be retired until the responsible operational owner verifies that its essential decisions, timing assumptions, and audit needs are supported in the target process.
S905: During shadow operations, local tools shall remain the authoritative source while the Regional Flow Platform produces parallel outputs for comparison by operational users.
S906: The cutover decision shall be based on measured agreement between local practice and Regional Flow Platform outputs, user confidence, defect closure, and demonstrated recovery from simulated failures.
S907: After cutover, local users shall enter operational decisions through the Airport CDM Portal and shall avoid reintroducing uncontrolled parallel records that undermine common situational awareness.
S908: The Contingency Operations Console shall be available at each onboarded airport before reliance on the Regional Flow Platform is declared for Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase, or Contingency Fallback State.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
